body.text: Why does AI bubble still shape capital allocation and market pricing across global desks? Behind the headline numbers lies a structural mechanism that quietly governs liquidity, risk, and long-term purchasing power.
Early AI investment was funded primarily with operating cash flow, but by 2026 the bond market came to dominate the AI build-out financing, as well as $3 trillion in off-balance-sheet commitments.

Speculation about a bubble also stems from concerns that leading AI tech firms are involved in a circular flow of investments that are artificially inflating the value of their stocks and the broader market. " Some, like hedge fund manager Ray Dalio, see other similarities with the dot-com bubble.

body.text: Due to the growing demand for semiconductors to sustain AI technologies, Nvidia in July 2025 became the first company in the world to reach a market value of $4 trillion. The figure had quadrupled since 2023, when it surpassed $1 trillion. 3% of the S&P 500, which hit an all-time high.

In October 2025, the company's value grew beyond $5 trillion, rising higher than the GDP of every country except for the United States and China, according to data from the World Bank. Over the year 2025, AI-related enterprises accounted for roughly 80% of gains in the American stock market.
Some skeptics warned that the rapid rise of AI tech firms may be the result of excessive financial engineering.

Microsoft disclosed that it had spent almost $35 billion on AI infrastructure in the three months leading up to the end of September. In October, it became the second-most-valuable company in the world, largely due to its 27% stake in OpenAI.
While seeing increases in revenue by 18% and in net income by 12%, share values dropped by 4% in after-hours trading amid investors' concerns about the possible costs of sustaining the AI boom.

In late 2025, 30% of the US S&P 500 and 20% of the MSCI World index was solely held up by the five largest companies (Nvidia, Microsoft, Apple, Alphabet, and Amazon), which was the greatest concentration in half a century, and share valuations were reportedly the most stretched since the dot-com bubble.

Experts warned that AI companies were extremely overvalued, with the S&P 500 trading at 23 times forward earnings, and the FTSE Index trading at 14 times, showing how expensive the US market had become. The Shiller price-to-earnings ratio for the US market also exceeded 40 for the first time since the dot-com crash.

18 trillion in market value due to a massive sell-off in Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix stocks (which together held more than half of the index value), triggered by Big Tech's lack of short-term return on investment in AI infrastructure, and fears of a subsequent slowdown in demand for High Bandwidth Memory chips.
In October, the Chinese index STAR50 had dropped 40% since July due to limitations on Chinese exports and limited demand, described by several organizations as the bursting of China's AI bubble.
By October 2026, the demand for AI computing power was exceeding supply, leading to increasing prices for capacity and what one start-up executive described as a "gold rush" mentality.

In November 2026, following the Jensen Huang scandal, increased spending on AI, and the widespread Democratic win in the midterms, the S&P 500 entered a correction, and both Nvidia's and Anthropic's stock dropped significantly. This has led to speculation about whether the AI bubble is bursting and what will be the downstream effects.

Analysis conducted in November 2026 by researchers at London Business School and Cambridge University showed results of large language models trained to analyze articles in The Economist dating to 1843. The analysis of about 486,000 market-relevant articles concluded there was roughly a 97% probability of an AI bubble in September 2026.
Speculation

In early 2025, Bridgewater Associates co-chief investment officer Ray Dalio said that the current levels of investment in AI are "very similar" to the dot-com bubble. Sam Altman, CEO of OpenAI, which created ChatGPT, said in August 2025 that he believed that an AI bubble exists.
In October 2025, Jamie Dimon, chief executive of JPMorgan Chase, the largest bank in the US, said he thinks "AI is real" but said he believes some money invested now will be wasted.
He also said there is a higher chance of a meaningful drop in stocks over the following two years than the market was reflecting.
Lack of profitability

Critics argue that the values of technology company stocks have been inflated based on AI hype regardless of market fundamentals or the financial reality behind monetizing AI products. 8%, leading to comparison with productivity paradox.

4 trillion over 8 years in building new data centers, partnering with Nvidia to deliver 10 gigawatts of data center computation, with just US$13 billion in revenue. This long-term spending is funded by debt.

An estimate from Morgan Stanley put global spending on datacenters between 2025 and 2028 at US$3 trillion, half of which is covered by private credit. In November 2025, OpenAI said it expected to report annual losses through 2028, including US$74 billion in operating losses in 2028 alone.

The Wall Street Journal obtained financial documents where OpenAI projects significant profits in 2030 despite preceding years of deep losses. Deutsche Bank analyst Jim Reid estimated OpenAI's losses amounting to US$140 billion between 2024 and 2029.
" OpenAI has been projected to run out of money by mid-2027.
AI build-out financing

Concerns were raised, notably by critic Ed Zitron, that leading AI tech firms were using circular financing and investment to artificially boost their valuations. In September, Nvidia announced a $100 billion investment into OpenAI, expanding the pre-existing stake that it held in the company.
This agreement was made on the expectation that OpenAI would power additional data centers using the GPUs that it had been buying from Nvidia, establishing a circular flow of money.

In October 2025, OpenAI purchased billions of dollars worth of graphics cards and CPUs from AMD, a rival of Nvidia, to supply its development of AI in an agreement that made it one of the largest shareholders in the company.
Microsoft also held a large stake in OpenAI, and Oracle Corporation, a computing company, also entered into a $300 billion deal with the company.

Hyperscalers had historically been net savers, flush with cash and little debt, but in 2026 they began aggressively selling long-dated bonds to finance AI, including a rare 100-year term bond from Alphabet.
The bonds were typically sold in non-USD currencies and in large denominations to attract pension fund and insurance company investors, using off-balance-sheet special-purpose vehicles.
The build-out is also enabled by private credit, a nearly $2 trillion part of the shadow banking system that operates outside the regulatory structure of the conventional banking system.

The Financial Stability Board, which monitors and advises the G20 financial system, warned in May 2026 that a “sharp correction in asset valuations, which have increased rapidly, could lead to sizeable credit losses to private credit investors,” as well as a risk of an investor "run" on private credit funds should their loans go bad.

Traditional banks have increasing risk exposure to private credit by directly lending to them or by other indirect means. By 2026, growing concerns about the stability of the industry drew comparisons to the lead-up to the 2008 financial crisis.

Oracle Corporation executive chairman Larry Ellison co-founded the joint venture Stargate Project with the CEOs of OpenAI and Softbank in January 2025. The project announced plans to spend $500 billion on AI build-out in several states, with Oracle issuing debt of at least $100 billion.

The project has encountered intensifying economic and environmental resistance from local communities. In September 2026 Oracle sent a force majeure notice to the developer of its Project Jupiter data center in New Mexico, in an effort to delay payments on the project. The developer is a unit of private credit lender Blue Owl Capital.

In March 2026, OpenAI abandoned expansion of the Stargate flagship data center in Abilene, Texas, with an anonymous source saying the company instead hopes to use next-generation Nvidia chips elsewhere. Banks and bond raters signaled concerns about Oracle's financial stability by marking down the value of its loans and downgrading its bonds in 2026.
